text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- The SPD remains strongest party in Hessen. Wins for CDU in Frankfurt in local elections. The FDP re-enters the local council in Frankfurt
- Tax revenues considerably smaller than planned, according to Bavarian finance minister
- BDI industry federation criticises Waigel's plans to implement tax reform in arrears. Industrialist Arend Oetker said total tax burden should not exceed 45 percent
- Industry federation representing small to middle-sized companies criticises proposal that reform of income tax should be paid for by raising valued added tax
HANDELSBLATT
- Industry prepared to accept taxation on night work, overtime and holiday work. A conflict between the coalition and the SPD over tax reform seems to have escalated.
- SPD and CDU have easy wins in local electons in Hessen. the SPD remain in the lead in a poll seen as a litmus test for Bonn
- Protests against nuclear waste shipments continue. Angela Merkel, Bonn's environment minister, signals readiness to compromise
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Peaceful protests against nuclear waste shipment to medium-term storage depot in northern Germany
- Wins for big parties in local elections in Hessen
- Presumably 4.8 million unemployed in February
- Every second heating oil trader is threatened
- Bavaria wants a stability pact between federal government in Bonn and German states for European monetary union
DIE WELT
- In Hessen local elections wins for SPD and CDU. Social Democrats remain strongest party in communes, Greens and FDP lose support
- BMW wants to turn Rover into a top brand name
- Farmers protest against nuclear waste shipment
- Unemployment figures go up further according to newspaper Bilm am Sonntag which reported that it was around 4.8 million in February
- Demonstration against exhibition about role of German army during World War Two
